Tests and test helpers must not be generic.

What The Standard says

“Simplicity” — The Standard requires code to remain simple and understandable to mainstream engineers. Concrete test fixtures keep the tested subject and its dependencies visible instead of hiding behavior behind generic test machinery. read it here.
“Unit Tests” — The Standard's canonical controller tests use concrete, subject-specific test classes and mocks. The analyser turns that repeated testing shape into an explicit prohibition on generic suites and helpers. read it here.

Why it matters

A test should describe one concrete production behaviour, and a generic test or helper obscures which contract it verifies. Concrete types keep failures, fixtures, and ownership traceable to the service under test.

Bad code example

// Violates STXTEST001: Tests and test helpers must not be generic.
class StudentServiceTests<TStudent> { }

Good code example

// Follows STXTEST001
class StudentServiceTests { }
